title: Proverbs Chapter 29 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 29 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 29 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 29.

questions.question: What happens to he who hardeneth his neck after being often reproved?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:1 states that he who hardeneth his neck shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

questions.question: When the righteous are in authority, what do the people do?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:2 indicates that when the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29, what does a man who loves wisdom do?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:3 states that whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father.

questions.question: What does the king establish by judgment?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:4 says that the king by judgment establisheth the land.

questions.question: A man that flattereth his neighbor spreads what?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:5 indicates that a man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.

questions.question: True or False: The righteous sing and rejoice in the transgression of an evil man.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:6 states that in the transgression of an evil man there is a snare, but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

questions.question: The righteous considereth the cause of whom?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:7 states that the righteous considereth the cause of the poor.

questions.question: True or False: Scornful men bring a city into a snare.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:8 indicates that scornful men bring a city into a snare.

questions.question: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, what is the result?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:9 states that whether the wise man rage or laugh, there is no rest.

questions.question: True or False: The bloodthirsty love the upright.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:10 indicates that the bloodthirsty hate the upright.

questions.question: What shall be established for the king that faithfully judgeth the poor?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:14 states that the king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.

questions.question: True or False: The fear of man brings safety.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:25 indicates that the fear of man bringeth a snare, but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.

questions.question: Which instruction comes first in Proverbs 29?
options: The king by judgment establisheth the land
A man that flattereth his neighbor spreadeth a net
He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck
questions.correctAnswer: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck
questions.explanation: The first instruction in Proverbs 29 is about he that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, found in Proverbs 29:1.

questions.question: What happens when the wicked are multiplied?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:16 states that when the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth.

questions.question: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become what?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:21 states that he that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 29 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 29 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:10 say about the bloodthirsty and the upright?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:10 states that 'The bloodthirsty hate the upright', indicating that those who are violent or ruthless oppose those who are just and moral. This contrasts with the behavior of the just, who seek the welfare of others.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29:11, what distinguishes a fool from a wise man?
options: A fool is quiet; a wise man speaks freely
A fool knows when to speak; a wise man keeps it in until later
A fool speaks all his mind; a wise man waits
A fool is patient; a wise man is hasty
questions.correctAnswer: A fool uttereth all his mind; a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:11 illustrates that a fool lacks discretion by speaking all his thoughts, while a wise man knows the value of restraint, indicating wisdom in timing and speech.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 29:12 relate to the behavior of a ruler and their servants?
options: A ruler who listens to truth has good servants
A ruler who listens to lies has wicked servants
A ruler's servants are always good
questions.correctAnswer: A ruler who listens to lies has wicked servants
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:12 states that 'If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked', emphasizing that a ruler's character influences those around him, leading to a corrupt environment in the presence of dishonesty.

questions.question: What promise is made in Proverbs 29:14 regarding the king who judges the poor faithfully?
options: His throne shall be established for a short time
His throne shall be established forever
His throne shall be taken away
questions.correctAnswer: His throne shall be established forever
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:14 indicates that a king who judiciously and compassionately rules over the poor will have a lasting reign, reflecting the importance of justice and mercy in leadership.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29:15, what are the effects of correction on a child?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:15 states that 'The rod and reproof give wisdom', highlighting that proper discipline is essential for a child's development and well-being, while neglect leads to shame.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Proverbs 29:16 regarding the multiplication of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:16 notes that 'When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth', suggesting that an increase in wickedness leads to greater sinfulness in society.

questions.question: What is the connection between Proverbs 29:17 and the well-being of a parent?
options: Correcting a child brings rest and delight
Correcting a child has no effect
questions.correctAnswer: Correcting a child brings rest and delight
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:17 emphasizes that 'Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul', showing the positive outcome of parental correction and guidance.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 29:18 describe the importance of vision?
options: Where there is no vision, the people perish
questions.correctAnswer: Where there is no vision, the people perish
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:18 states that 'Where there is no vision, the people perish', highlighting the necessity of guidance and purpose in life; without it, individuals lack direction.

questions.question: True or False: A foolish servant will respond to correction according to Proverbs 29:19.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:19 explains that 'A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer', indicating that mere words will not change a foolish servant's behavior.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 29:20 asserts that a man who is hasty in his words has less hope than a fool.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:20 indicates that 'Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him', showing that rash speech is more detrimental than foolishness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Proverbs 29:22, an angry man is peaceful and calm.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:22 states that 'An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression', indicating that anger leads to conflict rather than peace.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:25 suggest about trust in the LORD?
options: Trust in the LORD leads to fear
Trust in the LORD brings safety
Trust in the LORD causes confusion
Trust in the LORD is unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD brings safety
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:25 states that 'The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe', illustrating that reliance on God provides true security amidst fears.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29:27, what is the relationship between the unjust and the just?
options: The unjust is favored by the just
The unjust is an abomination to the just
The just are indifferent to the unjust
questions.correctAnswer: The unjust is an abomination to the just
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:27 declares that 'An unjust man is an abomination to the just', indicating a fundamental moral opposition between those who are just and those who are not.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 29 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 29.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29:19, how does a servant typically respond to correction?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:19 states that a servant will not be corrected by words because even if he understands, he will not respond, indicating a lack of willingness to accept correction.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:20 say about a man who is hasty in his words?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:20 suggests that there is more hope for a fool than for a man who is hasty in his words, implying that hasty speech is a sign of foolishness.

questions.question: What outcome is promised to one who brings up his servant delicately according to Proverbs 29:21?
options: He will have a loyal servant
questions.correctAnswer: He will have a loyal servant
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:21 indicates that one who delicately brings up his servant from a child will ultimately have him become his son, suggesting loyalty and close relationship.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29:22, what does an angry man do?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:22 states that an angry man stirs up strife, indicating that anger leads to conflict rather than resolution.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:23 say about pride?
options: It is a sign of success
questions.explanation: According to Proverbs 29:23, a man's pride shall bring him low, while honor upholds the humble, indicating the dangers of pride.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:25 say about the fear of man?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:25 states that the fear of man brings a snare, contrasting with trust in the LORD which offers safety.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29:26, where does every man's judgment come from?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:26 indicates that while many seek the ruler's favor, ultimately every man's judgment comes from the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 29:27 states that an unjust man is an abomination to the just.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:27 confirms that an unjust man is indeed an abomination to the just, highlighting the moral divide between the two.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 29:24 teaches that partnering with a thief is a wise decision.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:24 states that whosoever is partner with a thief hateth his own soul, indicating that it is unwise to partner with those who engage in theft.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of judgment coming from God as seen in Proverbs 29:26?
questions.explanation: Romans 14:10 discusses how we will all stand before the judgment seat of God, echoing the theme of divine judgment found in Proverbs 29:26.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book addresses the concept of pride leading to downfall, similar to Proverbs 29:23?
questions.explanation: Isaiah often addresses the theme of pride and its consequences, aligning with the warning found in Proverbs 29:23 about pride bringing low.

questions.question: In Proverbs 29:18, where there is no vision, what is stated to happen?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:18 states that where there is no vision, the people perish, emphasizing the importance of guidance and foresight.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Proverbs 29:18 to convey its message?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:18 uses parallelism by contrasting the absence of vision with the perishing of people, a common feature in Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: What Hebrew word for 'vision' in Proverbs 29:18 emphasizes prophetic insight and guidance?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Chazon' used in Proverbs 29:18 refers to prophetic vision or revelation, which is crucial for leadership and guidance.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 29 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 29 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:1 teach about the consequences of ignoring correction?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:1 states that a person who hardens their neck against reproof will face destruction without remedy, emphasizing the serious consequences of rejecting correction.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 29:2, what is the effect of righteous authority on the people?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:2 indicates that when the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice, highlighting the positive impact of just leadership on society.

questions.question: What is the outcome for a man who keeps company with harlots, according to Proverbs 29:3?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:3 warns that associating with harlots leads to wastefulness, as he that keeps company with them will spend his substance.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:4 reveal about the role of judgment in establishing the land?
questions.explanation: According to Proverbs 29:4, a king who judges righteously establishes the land, indicating the importance of justice in governance.

questions.question: What is the consequence of flattering one's neighbor as mentioned in Proverbs 29:5?
options: It spreads a net for his feet
questions.correctAnswer: It spreads a net for his feet
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:5 explains that flattery can be deceptive and traps a person, likening it to spreading a net.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:16 suggest about the relationship between the wicked and transgression?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:16 states that when the wicked are multiplied, transgression increases, highlighting the correlation between wickedness and moral decline.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 29:18 describe the importance of vision for the people?
questions.explanation: According to Proverbs 29:18, without vision, the people perish, illustrating the necessity of divine guidance and purpose for a thriving society.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:23 say about pride and humility?
options: A man's pride shall bring him low
questions.correctAnswer: A man's pride shall bring him low
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:23 teaches that pride leads to downfall, while honor uplifts the humble, emphasizing the value of humility.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by His judgment in Proverbs 29:14?
questions.explanation: In Proverbs 29:14, the king who judges the poor faithfully reflects God's attribute of justice, as He cares for the marginalized and upholds righteousness.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:10 indicate about the relationship between the bloodthirsty and the upright?
options: They are indifferent to each other
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:10 states that the bloodthirsty hate those who are upright, illustrating the conflict between wickedness and righteousness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that all authority is corrupt and untrustworthy. What does Proverbs 29:12 teach?
options: Rulers who listen to lies are wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Rulers who listen to lies are wicked
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:12 teaches that a ruler who hearkens to lies causes wickedness among his servants, affirming that while authority can be corrupt, it must be held accountable to truth.

questions.question: What insight does Proverbs 29:6 provide about the emotional state of the righteous compared to the wicked?
questions.explanation: In Proverbs 29:6, the righteous are depicted as singing and rejoicing, contrasting their emotional state with that of the wicked, who are ensnared by their transgressions.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 29:24 describe the consequence of partnering with a thief?
options: It is good for the soul
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:24 indicates that being a partner with a thief ultimately harms oneself, highlighting the moral implications of unethical associations.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Proverbs 29:17 and 29:18 convey about parenting and vision?
options: Correcting children leads to their destruction
Correcting your son brings rest and vision prevents perishing
questions.correctAnswer: Correcting your son brings rest and vision prevents perishing
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:17 emphasizes the importance of correction in parenting, which yields rest, while 29:18 stresses that vision is critical to prevent perishing, thus combining the need for guidance and correction in raising children.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 29:19 teach about communication with a servant?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 29:19 states that a servant will not be corrected by mere words, indicating a limitation in communication when addressing those under authority.
